atoms.b: The answer to a division can ((++always never)) be written as a fraction.

For example, <mat><t-yellow>1</t-yellow> ÷ <t-purple>2</t-purple></mat> can either be written as the decimal number <mat><gap>++0.5 0.9 0.4</gap></mat>, or as the fraction <mat><gap>++<t-yellow>1</t-yellow>/<t-purple>2</t-purple> <t-yellow>1</t-yellow>/<t-purple>4</t-purple> <t-yellow>1</t-yellow>/<t-purple>3</t-purple></gap></mat>.
atoms.sound: For example, 1 ÷ 2 can either be written as the decimal number 0.5, or as the fraction 1 half.

atoms.b: To write a division as a fraction, the ((++<t-yellow>dividend</t-yellow> <t-purple>divisor</t-purple>)) becomes the <t-yellow>numerator</t-yellow> and the <t-purple>divisor</t-purple> becomes the ((++<t-purple>denominator</t-purple> <t-yellow>numerator</t-yellow>)).

hint.text: The <t-yellow>dividend</t-yellow> is the first number in a division and the <t-purple>divisor</t-purple> is the second number.
